rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating certain days as ill-omened and avoiding desired pursuits can strengthen piety; disregarding the concern and following every desire can violate religious respect, making the misfortune spiritual and conventionally linked to those days.
rows.anchor: فتؤول نحوسة هذه الأيام إلى جهات من الشقاء المعنوي

rows.speaker: الإمام العسكري
rows.claim: In a report from Sahl b. Yaqub, al-Askari tells him that the Imams’ loyal followers are protected by their allegiance, urges trust in God, and prescribes Quran and prayer to ward off omens.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن يعقوب الملقب بأبي نواس عن العسكري عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو إبراهيم
rows.claim: Muhammad b. Riyah al-Fallah reports seeing Abu Ibrahim cup on Friday; he is told to recite Ayat al-Kursi if blood surges, by day or night, and then cup.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن رياح الفلاح قال رأيت أبا إبراهيم عليه السلام يحتجم يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الثاني
rows.claim: In a reply to a question about traveling on Wednesday, Abu al-Hasan II says going that day in defiance of omen-believers protects from every affliction, cures illness, and fulfills the traveler’s need.
rows.anchor: من خرج يوم الأربعاء لا تدور خلافا على أهل الطيرة وقي من كل آفة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الثاني
rows.claim: Asked about cupping on Wednesday, Abu al-Hasan II says doing so against omen-believers protects from affliction and illness and keeps the cups from turning green.
rows.anchor: من احتجم في يوم الأربعاء لا تدور خلافا على أهل الطيرة عوفي من كل آفة

rows.speaker: الحسين بن مسعود
rows.claim: Husayn b. Masud recounts injuries, a collision, and torn clothes on a day he called ill-omened while visiting Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين بن مسعود دخلت على أبي الحسن علي بن محمد عليه السلام وقد نكبت إصبعي

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن علي بن محمد
rows.claim: Ali b. Muhammad rebukes Hasan for blaming the day: days have no agency, and people are repaid for their deeds; God alone rewards, punishes, and judges, so one must not attribute action to days.
rows.anchor: يا حسن ما ذنب الأيام حتى صرتم تتشاءمون بها إذا جوزيتم بأعمالكم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author infers that ill-omened days acquire their effect from popular superstition and its psychological influence; the reports counter it by redirecting the mind or, when needed, prescribing reliance on God, Quran, or prayer.
rows.anchor: وهذه الروايات تعالج نحوستها التي تأتيها من قبل الطيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author considers it plausible that reports affirming unlucky days were issued by dissimulation, since omens about times and places were widespread and reports attributed to the Prophet circulated even among early elites.
rows.anchor: وحمل بعضهم هذه الروايات المسلمة لنحوسة بعض الأيام على التقية، وليس بذاك البعيد

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report transmitted by al-Fadl b. al-Rabi from al-Mamun and earlier rulers attributes to the Prophet the statement that the last Wednesday of a month is persistently ill-omened; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: إن آخر الأربعاء في الشهر يوم نحس مستمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about fortunate days are explained like those about unlucky days: religiously valued events, such as the Prophet’s birth and mission, make the day blessed in religious sensibility.
rows.anchor: تعليل بركة ما عده من الأيام السعيدة بوقوع حوادث متبركة عظيمة في نظر الدين

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that his community be blessed in its early activity on Saturdays and Thursdays.
rows.anchor: اللهم بارك لأمتي في بكورها يوم سبتها وخميسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the report that God softened iron for David on Tuesday as an example used to explain a day’s religiously favorable association.
rows.anchor: أن الله ألان الحديد لداود عليه السلام يوم الثلاثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes a report that the Prophet used to set out on journeys on Friday.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يخرج للسفر يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also cites Sunday as one of God’s names among explanations for fortunate-day reports.
rows.anchor: وأن الأحد من أسماء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports on fortunate and unfortunate days indicate religiously significant events or psychological effects, not an inherent lucky or unlucky quality rooted in the time’s natural constitution; apparently contrary reports are dissimulative or unreliable.
rows.anchor: لا تدل على أزيد من ابتنائهما على حوادث مرتبطة بالدين توجب حسنا وقبحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason cannot prove astrological good or bad fortune, such as the Sun or Jupiter being auspicious, Mars inauspicious, or particular planetary conjunctions having those qualities.
rows.anchor: فلا سبيل إلى إقامة البرهان على شيء من ذلك كسعادة الشمس والمشتري

rows.speaker: منجمو الهند
rows.claim: Ancient Indian astrologers held that earthly events are linked to all celestial configurations, including both fixed stars and planets.
rows.anchor: كان القدماء من منجمي الهند يرون للحوادث الأرضية ارتباطا بالأوضاع السماوية مطلقا

rows.speaker: غيرهم
rows.claim: Other astrologers restricted the connection to configurations of the seven planets, excluding the fixed stars, and assigned effects to their different arrangements.
rows.anchor: وغيرهم يرى ذلك بين الحوادث وبين أوضاع السيارات السبع دون الثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account makes celestial bodies living, willing beings that act as efficient causes of events below.
rows.anchor: الأجرام الكوكبية موجودات ذوات نفوس حية مريدة تفعل أفاعيلها بالعلية الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account treats the stars as soulless bodies that nevertheless act as efficient causes.
rows.anchor: بأنها أجرام غير ذات نفس تؤثر أثرها بالعلية الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes celestial bodies or their configurations instruments preparing events while God remains their agent.
rows.anchor: أو هي معدات لفعله تعالى وهو الفاعل للحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view regards the stars and their configurations only as signs of events, without causing or preparing them.
rows.anchor: أو أن الكواكب وأوضاعها علامات للحوادث من غير فاعلية ولا إعداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final view denies even a sign-like connection, holding that God merely customarily brings an event about at a certain celestial configuration.
rows.anchor: وإنما جرت عادة الله على أن يحدث حادثة كذا عند وضع سماوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astrological rules are not invariably predictive; anecdotes and some Imami reports suggest a limited connection between celestial configurations and earthly events, but not a universal one.
rows.anchor: يعطي أن بين الأوضاع السماوية والحوادث الأرضية ارتباطا ما إلا أنه في الجملة لا بالجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cannot definitively label a particular star or configuration auspicious or inauspicious, though a connection between celestial configurations and earthly events cannot be denied.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن الحكم البتي بكون كوكب كذا أو وضع كذا سعدا أو نحسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Celestial influence subordinate to God is not inherently against religious essentials; claiming that stars create independently of God or govern the cosmos independently would be shirk and entail worship.
rows.anchor: أو أن يقال بكونها مدبرة للنظام الكوني مستقلة في التدبير فيكون ربوبية

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: The Golden Epistle attributed to al-Rida says intercourse with the Moon in Aries or Aquarius is best, and Taurus is better still because the Moon is exalted there.
rows.anchor: عن الرضا عليه السلام اعلم أن جماعهن والقمر في برج الحمل أو الدلو من البروج أفضل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Humran says that one who travels or marries while the Moon is in Scorpio will not see good fortune.
rows.anchor: عن حمران عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من سافر أو تزوج والقمر في العقرب لم ير الحسنى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report in Ibn Tawus’s Book of Astrology says Ali disliked traveling during the dark moon or when the Moon was in Scorpio.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام يكره أن يسافر الرجل في محاق الشهر وإذا كان القمر في العقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests reports apparently affirming astrological fortunes may reflect dissimulation, popular superstition, or a special relation in which a celestial configuration is only a potential condition for an earthly event.
rows.anchor: على ما قيل، أو على مقارنة الطيرة العامة

rows.speaker: موسى بن جعفر
rows.claim: A report from Musa b. Jafar and his forebears recommends charity in the morning or evening to remove that day’s or night’s ill omen, which the author sees as possibly supporting a conditional celestial link.
rows.anchor: عن موسى بن جعفر عن أبيه عن جده في حديث إذا أصبحت فتصدق بصدقة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Nahj al-Balagha compares the astrologer to a soothsayer and sorcerer and condemns such practice as unbelief leading to the Fire.
rows.anchor: المنجم كالكاهن والكاهن كالساحر والساحر كالكافر والكافر في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports permitting study and affirming astrology suggest that the ban targets reliance on astrology as independently effective, since that belief would lead to shirk.
rows.anchor: إنما هو فيما اعتقد لها استقلال في التأثير لتأديته إلى الشرك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman b. Sayaba asks al-Sadiq whether studying stars harms religion; he replies it does not, but much of the knowledge cannot be attained and a little is of no benefit.
rows.anchor: إنكم تنظرون في شيء منها كثيره لا يدرك وقليله لا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked whether astrology is true, al-Sadiq answers yes and says people on earth know it; other reports restrict that knowledge to a few Indian and Arab, or Qurayshi, families.
rows.anchor: وفي عدة من الروايات ما يعلمها إلا أهل بيت من الهند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports on astrology support the author’s conclusion that celestial configurations and their judgments have some connection, without establishing a universal deterministic rule.
rows.anchor: وهذه الروايات تؤيد ما قدمناه من أن بين الأوضاع والأحكام ارتباطا ما في الجملة

rows.speaker: المشتري
rows.claim: A story says Jupiter appeared on earth as a man, taught astrology first to a Persian and then an Indian, whose calculation identified his teacher as Jupiter; the teacher died in shock and his family inherited the knowledge.
rows.anchor: أن الله أنزل المشتري على الأرض في صورة رجل فلقي رجلا من العجم فعلمه النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author regards the Jupiter teaching story as resembling a fabrication.
rows.anchor: وهو أشبه بالموضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Optimism is taking an event as a sign and anticipating good; superstition is taking it as a sign of evil, and both often affect outcomes psychologically, especially in the case of evil expectation.
rows.anchor: وهما الاستدلال بحادث من الحوادث على الخير وترقبه وهو التفاؤل أو على الشر وهو التطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam distinguishes the two by encouraging optimism and forbidding superstition, which confirms that their effect is psychological.
rows.anchor: أما التفاؤل ففيما روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have urged people to expect good, and the author says he often showed optimism in many situations.
rows.anchor: تفاءلوا بالخير تجدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran depicts earlier peoples rejecting their prophets after claiming the prophets brought bad omens; the prophets answer that omens cannot overturn truth and that good and evil belong to God, not to a bird powerless even over itself.
rows.anchor: وأن الأمر إلى الله سبحانه لا إلى الطائر الذي لا يملك لنفسه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the exchange at 36:18–19, the messengers answer that the people’s evil omen is with themselves, not with the messengers.
rows.anchor: أي ما يجر إليكم الشر هو معكم لا معنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 27:47, the answer that the people’s omen is with God means God alone determines what brings them good or evil.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يأتيكم به الخير أو الشر عند الله فهو الذي يقدر فيكم ما يقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports forbid superstition and advise dismissing its effect or warding it off through trust and prayer, supporting the view that its force is psychological.
rows.anchor: وقد وردت أخبار كثيرة في النهي عن الطيرة وفي دفع شؤمها بعدم الاعتناء أو بالتوكل والدعاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Amr b. Hurayth reports al-Sadiq saying an omen has only the force a person gives it: minimize it and it diminishes, intensify it and it grows, ignore it and it is nothing.
rows.anchor: الطيرة على ما تجعلها إن هونتها تهونت

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A hadith transmitted through Sunni routes says no one escapes superstition, envy, and suspicion; respond by proceeding after an omen, avoiding transgression when envious, and not confirming suspicion.
rows.anchor: ثلاث لا يسلم منها أحد الطيرة والحسد والظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question ‘what, no defenders?’ and the following boast mean the unbelievers think they are united, can retaliate against attackers, and can support one another so they will not be defeated.
rows.anchor: أي الكفار نحن قوم مجتمعون متحدون ننتقم ممن أرادنا بسوء أو ينصر بعضنا بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in ‘the gathering’ points back to the group just mentioned; ‘the back’ is generic, and turning one’s back means retreating.
rows.anchor: اللام في { الجمع } للعهد الذكري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse predicts that the boastful group will be defeated and flee from an impending battle; this Quranic prediction came true at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقع ذلك في غزاة بدر، وهذا من ملاحم القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘More calamitous’ intensifies a dire affliction with no escape, while ‘more bitter’ means more bitter, the opposite of sweet.
rows.anchor: اسم تفضيل من الدهاء وهو عظم البلية المنكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning shifts from worldly defeat and punishment to the Hour, which is worse than every calamity and more bitter than any bitter thing.
rows.anchor: إضراب عن إيعادهم بالانهزام والعذاب الدنيوي إلى إيعادهم بما سيجري عليهم في الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are in error away from the abode of happiness, Paradise, and in blazing fires; this explains why the Hour is more dire and bitter for them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم مجرمون والمجرمون في ضلال عن موطن السعادة وهو الجنة ونيران مسعرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being dragged means being pulled along on one’s face; ‘the day’ is a temporal adverb for their state in error and fire, Saqar is a name of Hell, and its touch is the burning heat and punishment.
rows.anchor: السحب جر الإنسان على وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Everything’ is the object of an implicit verb supplied by ‘We created’; the preposition in ‘by measure’ attaches to ‘created,’ and the bāʾ indicates accompaniment.
rows.anchor: والتقدير خلقنا كل شيء خلقناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadar is each thing’s determined measure and limit, which it cannot exceed in either increase or decrease.
rows.anchor: وقدر الشيء هو المقدار الذي لا يتعداه والحد والهندسة التي لا يتجاوزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As 15:21 says that everything is held in God’s treasuries and sent down by a known measure, every thing has a defined limit and a path it follows in existence.
rows.anchor: فلكل شيء حد محدود في خلقه لا يتعداه وصراط ممدود في وجوده يسلكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The measure answers why criminals are punished: human beings are a reproducing social species made for transient worldly life and eternal life beyond it; God sends messengers, and accepting or rejecting their call is measured to lead to Paradise or punishment.
rows.anchor: فمن استجاب الدعوة فاز بالسعادة ودخل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is not circular: human actions follow general rules inferred from external existence and learned effects, such as eating to satisfy hunger and drinking to quench thirst.
rows.anchor: فإنا نتبع في أفعالنا القوانين والأصول الكلية المأخوذة من الكون الخارجي والوجود العيني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s acts are not governed by an external cause or prior universal rational rule: such rules are derived from His act and are subordinate to it, as the cited verses affirm.
rows.anchor: فلا سؤال عن فعله تعالى بلم بمعنى السؤال عن السبب الخارجي إذ لا سبب دونه يعينه في فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, God’s acts can be explained by their benefits to creatures; this explains the act within causal relations, not why God acts as God. The author illustrates this with the cited verses on Christian affection and Israel’s humiliation.
rows.anchor: تعليل الفعل بما يترتب عليه من الغايات والفوائد العائدة إلى الخلق لا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, a particular act can be explained through a fitting divine name or attribute; such active names are drawn from God’s general acts, so the particular is explained by a general feature of divine action.
rows.anchor: تعليل فعله تعالى بشيء من أسمائه وصفاته المناسبة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, the specific punishment in 54:47–49 is explained by God’s general act of measuring all things: the criminal’s punishment is one instance of the measure set for a person who rejects prophecy.
rows.anchor: فإن القدر وهو كون الشيء محدودا لا يتخطى حده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran describes creation as measured and guided in several formulations: God measured everything, gave each thing its form and then guided it, and holds all things in measure.
rows.anchor: وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadar has two levels: a universal limit on the possible, dependent existence of every being except God, and a particular limit on observable beings shaped by their causes and conditions.
rows.anchor: للتقدير مرتبتين مرتبة تعم جميع ما سوى الله وهي تحديد أصل الوجود بالإمكان والحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the observable world, external and internal causes and conditions shape each thing’s existence, effects, form, dimensions, states, and actions; this measure guides it along its assigned course.
rows.anchor: فهي مقلوبة بقوالب من داخل وخارج تعين لها من العرض والطول والشكل والهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God created, proportioned, measured, and guided each thing means He guides what He created along the course measured for it.
rows.anchor: أي هدى ما خلقه إلى ما قدر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For human beings, being created from a drop, measured, and then having the path made easy shows that qadar does not negate voluntary action.
rows.anchor: ويشير بقوله { ثم السبيل يسره } إلى أن التقدير لا ينافي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This form of qadar differs from qada, God’s decisive judgment that something exist, which no one can reverse.
rows.anchor: وهذا النوع من القدر في نفسه غير القضاء الذي هو الحكم البتي منه تعالى بوجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A measure implied by some causes or conditions may fail to reach actualization because an impediment intervenes or another cause replaces it; the Quran calls this erasing and confirming.
rows.anchor: فربما قدر ولم يعقبه القضاء كالقدر الذي يقتضيه بعض العلل والشرائط الخارجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When every cause and condition is assembled and all impediments are absent, qadar is followed by qada.
rows.anchor: وربما قدر وتبعه القضاء كما إذا قدر من جميع الجهات باجتماع جميع علله وشرائطه وارتفاع موانعه

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: A report in al-Mahasin says that when God decrees something He carries it out, and that outcome cannot be averted; other reports likewise distinguish changeable qadar from irreversible qada.
rows.anchor: إذا قضى أمضاه فذلك الذي لا مرد له

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ibn Nubata reports that when Ali moved from a leaning wall to another, he answered that he was fleeing God’s qada to God’s qadar.
rows.anchor: أفر من قضاء الله إلى قدر الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For beings whose measure is only the limit of possibility and need, qadar and qada are identical and the measure necessarily comes to pass.
rows.anchor: فالقدر والقضاء فيه واحد ولا يتخلف القدر فيه عن التحقق البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rationally, each element of a composite cause (agent, matter, conditions, preparations, and impediments) contributes a matching effect that shapes the thing’s measure; when the complete cause forms, existence becomes necessary, which is qada.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي القضاء الذي لا مرد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a useful earlier discussion of qada, the author refers readers to his commentary at the beginning of Surat al-Isra.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير أول سورة الإسراء كلام في القضاء
